criteria.statement: Get, GetInt, GetBool and GetDuration all call one unexported method lookup(section, key string) (string, error), and none of them reads c.sections directly
The exported API, every returned value and every error message of the four getters are exactly as before the refactor

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-3dafdc2a9bc44f02)

goal:
`getters.go` repeats the same section-and-key lookup in `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration`. Move it into one unexported method,

```go
func (c *Config) lookup(section, key string) (string, error)
```

and make all four getters use it, so that none of them reads `c.sections` directly any more.

This is a pure refactor. The exported API, every returned value and every error message must stay exactly as they are now. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

previous_result.summary:
I added `lookup(section, key string) (string, error)` to `getters.go`, and `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration` now all call it. Only `lookup` reads `c.sections` now.

`GetBool` reports a missing key as `key %q not set`, while the other three say `no key %q`. To keep both wordings exact, `lookup` returns an unexported `noKeyError`, and `GetBool` detects it and rewrites the message.

`go vet ./...` is clean and `go test ./...` passes (interlock run run-3e58ac7147e349d6). I recorded the `behaviour` claim as static only, so interlock warned it needs a tested claim. I did not add a test for the `GetBool` missing-key message, so that wording is checked by reading the code only.
